newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Chiluba sworn in for 2nd term as Zambian president.
newsitem.headline: Chiluba sworn in for 2nd term as Zambian president.

text.p: Frederick Chiluba was sworn in as president of Zambia for a second five-year term on Thursday after a landslide win in Zambia's presidential elections, officials said.

Not all results were in by Thursday afternoon when Chiluba took his oath of office after, as expected, winning Monday's poll which was boycotted by major opposition parties, including that of main rival "Father of the Nation" Kenneth Kaunda.
Election officials announced that results in from 138 of the country's 150 constituencies had given Chiluba roughly 70 percent of the 1.19 million ballots counted.
His closest rival, Zambia Democratic Congress leader Dean Mungomba, took 144,366 votes.
Chiluba and his ruling Movement for Multi-party Democracy had been expected to win decisively in the disputed election, marked by the opposition boycott and a low turnout.

Two groups monitoring the election gave conflicting views of the ballot. A Zambian group said the election was neither free nor fair since half of eligible voters were unfairly excluded but an international group said it found the balloting generally correct.
